speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Archaeological finds and records show that Singapore’s history stretches back at least 700 years, serving as a trading emporium in the region.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The year 1819 was a key turning point in Singapore's development.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This, and subsequent developments, transformed Singapore into a global node.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In our bicentennial year, let us reflect on the twists and turns in our history so as to chart a path forward for an even better future for our people.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Today, we are in a different phase of globalisation, with new forces reshaping the global environment.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In last year's Budget Statement, I mentioned three major shifts: (a) the shift in global economic weight towards Asia; (b) rapid technological advancements; (c) and changing demographic patterns.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some countries are benefiting from globalisation, while others are questioning its value.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These four major forces are interacting in complex ways, at the global, regional and national levels.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Closer to home, ASEAN has enjoyed over 50 years of peace and stability, with bright economic prospects.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In recent years, Southeast Asia has grown several new "unicorns", or companies with valuations in excess of US$1 billion.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Working together, ASEAN nations can maximise our potential.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But, closely connected neighbours will have occasional differences.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: When such differences occur, Singaporeans must stay united as a people and present our positions firmly and calmly.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have worked through difficult bilateral issues with our neighbours in the past, based on mutual respect and common interests and in accordance with international laws and norms.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singapore will continue to seek to resolve issues in the same spirit.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Domestically, we need to address longer-term challenges, including ageing, social mobility, inequality, economic transformation and climate change.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The changing global and domestic landscape presents both challenges and opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will continue to chart our way forward confidently in the Singapore way, building on our distinct strengths and our Singaporean DNA.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must respond to challenges with grit and determination.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There were episodes in the centuries of Singapore's history where our island’s fortunes waned due to external forces.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These are sobering reminders that we have to constantly build up our security and resilience, and plan long term.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singapore's success has roots in our port, which thrives on openness and connectivity.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These traits have been forged into our identity as a people.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As a multicultural society, our openness to diversity is our strength.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It has inculcated a global mindset and deepened our knowledge of Asia.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must continue to cultivate cross-cultural literacy among our youth and encourage them to build bridges with peoples across the world.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We strive to be a place where people and ideas congregate at the frontier of global developments.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We want to be a Global-Asia node of technology, innovation and enterprise.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We turn our size and strategic location into an advantage.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Technological shifts have spread economic activities more widely and, at the same time, made cities more important as key nodes of enterprise and innovation.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As a city-state, we are nimbler and can adapt to changes faster.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We serve as a neutral, trusted node in key spheres of global activity.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Like Sang Kancil, the small but quick-witted mousedeer, we can make our way in the world.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In this bicentennial year, let us draw on our strengths, and our Singaporean DNA – openness, multiculturalism, and self-determination – to continue to progress.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: At a fundamental level, we must keep Singapore safe and secure.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This allows us to preserve our way of life and forge our own destiny.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must continue to transform our economy, for only a vibrant and innovative economy can provide opportunities for our people to realise their potential.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must continue to build a caring and inclusive society, one where we look out for one another, and all of us play our part in weaving a tightly knit social fabric.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must continue to build Singapore as a global city and home for all, keeping it smart, sustainable and globally connected.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Last but not least, we must achieve these goals in a responsible and fiscally sustainable way.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are using our financial resources to help realise our strategies for a strong, united Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But financial resources alone do not get us there.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We call on all Singaporeans to partner with the Government and support one another to succeed in this endeavour.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A safe and secure Singapore gives us the confidence to chart an independent course.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But we cannot take our peace, prosperity and stability for granted.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singapore is vulnerable to the fluctuations in our region and the world.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Against an increasingly uncertain geopolitical environment, our commitment to defence and security cannot waver.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Diplomacy and deterrence are the twin pillars of our approach.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) works continuously to build good relations with our neighbours and the major powers and to promote a rules-based international order with international laws and norms.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A strong Singapore Armed Forces (SAF) lends weight to our diplomatic efforts and ensures that negotiations with Singapore are taken seriously.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Should diplomacy fail, we must stand ready to safeguard our interests and defend ourselves.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Home Team also works round-the-clock alongside other security agencies, to ensure a safe environment for all.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We also now have the Cyber Security Agency of Singapore leading our efforts to protect our Critical Information Infrastructure from cyber threats, and to create a secure cyberspace for businesses and communities.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These are fundamental to our sovereignty, our success and to safeguarding our vital interests.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singapore is one of the safest cities in the world.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our crime rates are consistently low, but we must not be complacent.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Security threats are evolving and becoming more complex.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A strong SAF remains a bulwark against threats to our way of life.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We continue to detect individuals in Singapore who have been radicalised by terrorist propaganda.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Globally, we see a rise in attacks perpetrated by radicalised individuals and cells.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Beyond physical threats, malicious cyber activities are growing.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The networked nature of our society has enhanced connectivity.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But this can be exploited to disrupt and divide society through cyberattacks, the spread of falsehoods or other means.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In particular, foreign actors will try to influence our domestic affairs and politics.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is not new, but new technologies have made it easier for others to mount attacks with greater ease and intensity and with more sophisticated tactics.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To stay ahead of these threats, we must continue to innovate and build new capabilities to meet our security needs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Both the public and private sectors have a major role to play.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These capabilities will strengthen the Home Team’s ability to carry out its mission of safeguarding Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Minister for Home Affairs will speak more about this at the Committee of Supply (COS).

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The private security industry has been stepping up efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A good example is Certis, which has redesigned its business processes, infusing technologies such as big data and artificial intelligence (AI) to deal with security threats.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: MHA will also help to transform the private security industry through innovation and technology to meet growing needs and be an effective partner to the Home Team.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our Total Defence approach will continue to keep Singapore safe and secure, with every Singaporean playing a part.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: At the national level, we plan long-term and take measures, such as stockpiling critical supplies, diversifying our sources of water supply, and strengthening our food security.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As a people, we must have the psychological and emotional resilience to face crises stoically.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As threats get more sophisticated, Singaporeans must stay vigilant and guard against non-conventional forces that threaten to divide us.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: National Service (NS) has forged a deep understanding in our people that each and every one of us has the duty to defend our nation.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: When our young people serve NS, families and employers support them in every way possible.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With our Smart Nation drive, digital technology has become an integral part of our lives.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To harness the digital advantage, we must be prepared to also deal with the threats that arise inevitably from its more pervasive use.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Like the other pillars of Total Defence, Digital Defence involves everyone – individuals, community groups, businesses and the Government.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must all play our part to be secure, alert and responsible online, be it through practising good cyber hygiene, being vigilant against fake news and helping one another use technology safely.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government is also engaging our tech community with programmes, such as the Government Bug Bounty Programme, to achieve a higher level of collective cybersecurity.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will invest more, if the need arises, to protect the sovereignty of Singapore and the well-being of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Everyone has a role to play to keep Singapore safe and secure.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Let us continue to stay united in defending our home and our way of life.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A vibrant and innovative economy provides our people with the opportunities to realise their potential and to have a better life.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our efforts to transform our economy are bearing fruit.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Good growth translated into good outcomes for our workers.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Global growth is expected to moderate in 2019, while uncertainties and downside risks in the global economy have increased.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Over the years, our sound monetary and fiscal policies have enabled us to weather global economic crises and keep inflation stable.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These provide a stable environment for investors to make long-term investment decisions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Beyond maintaining a supportive macroeconomic environment, we need to build a sound microeconomic foundation, so that resources can be allocated to their best possible uses and to undertake structural reforms to enable our workers and firms to adapt and stay competitive.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Every firm and every worker will need to work differently, master new skills and use technology well.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And we must continue to create new opportunities, including through partnerships with others.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Each ITM integrates four key pillars of transformation: jobs and skills; innovation; internationalisation; and productivity.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These are mutually reinforcing pillars to maximise impact.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To coordinate efforts, the Future Economy Council brings together leaders from the Government, industry, trade associations and chambers (TACs), unions and academia.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are seeing good progress, aided by the global economic upturn in recent years.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In particular, we have seen strong performance by outward-oriented sectors such as manufacturing, while others like construction and some services industries continue to show weaker productivity growth.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There is much more we can do, especially in sectors like domestic services.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The basic building blocks of a vibrant economy are strong, competitive companies that maximise value creation.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Hence, the first thrust is to support the building of deep enterprise capabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Companies at different stages of growth have different needs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The leadership of each company is in the best position to lead and drive changes, while our agencies can provide support at each stage of growth.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A vibrant start-up ecosystem encourages budding entrepreneurs to try out their business ideas.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Such an ecosystem enables entrepreneurs to connect to mentors, prospective business partners, customers, and investors.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Two years ago, we launched Startup SG to provide holistic support for start-ups and entrepreneurs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is a significant rise from the 80 deals worth US$136 million in 2012.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Today, more than 150 global venture capital funds, incubators, and accelerators are based in Singapore, supporting start-ups here and in the region.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Start-ups can only thrive if they scale up and venture into new markets.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To help them do so, we will provide support in three areas: providing customised assistance, better financing options, and supporting technology adoption.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Customised support can enable firms to identify and overcome the unique challenges they face and scale up quickly.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Enterprise Singapore will launch a Scale-up SG programme in partnership with the private and public sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Scale-up SG will work with aspiring, high-growth local firms to identify and build new capabilities, to innovate, grow, and internationalise.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To support innovation, we will launch a pilot Innovation Agents programme, for firms to tap on a pool of experts to advise them on opportunities to innovate and commercialise technology.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Having smart, patient capital that attracts investors with the expertise and the right time horizon is another way to help firms scale-up.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Over the past few years, the Government has worked on improving access to private capital for start-ups and small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs).

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The pool of private equity and venture capital managers in Singapore has grown.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) has simplified the regulatory regime for venture capital managers and launched a US$5 billion private markets programme to encourage global private equity players to deepen their presence here.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To further deepen the pool of smart, patient capital, the Government has, since 2010, set aside $400 million through two rounds of fund injections for the Co-Investment Programme (CIP) to invest in our SMEs, alongside the private sector.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Loan financing remains an important source of funding for SMEs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: DBS provides a Business Capabilities Loan for innovative SME projects, UOB provides financial support for technology investments and overseas ventures, while OCBC finances new SMEs which lack the track record typically required for credit assessment.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To catalyse these further, we will enhance the accessibility of loans.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Today, our economic agencies have different financing schemes.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will be launched in October this year.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In addition, the Enterprise Financing Scheme will provide stronger support for companies that have been incorporated for less than five years.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Support for working capital will be folded under the Enterprise Financing Scheme from October.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our companies and workers must stay on top of rapid advances in technology, especially in digital technology.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will continue to help our SMEs adopt digital technologies.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We launched the SMEs Go Digital programme in Budget 2017.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Since then, around 4,000 SMEs have adopted pre-approved digital solutions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will expand the SMEs Go Digital programme.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These will guide SMEs on relevant digital technologies and skills training programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, we will expand the number and range of cost-effective, pre-approved digital solutions that will be supported under SMEs Go Digital, to boost technology adoption among SMEs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To help companies in the services sector capture opportunities from digitalisation, the Ministry of Communications and Information launched a pilot of the Digital Services Lab (DSL) in November last year.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The DSL brings together industry and the research community, to co-develop digital solutions with sector-wide impact.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, the DSL is exploring the development of solutions to integrate the logistics chain for retail in malls.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Besides digital technology, we will support our firms to integrate technologies and re-engineer business processes to raise efficiency and enhance product development.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Last year, I announced the Productivity Solutions Grant (PSG), to help firms adopt off-the-shelf technology.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This year, we will extend the Automation Support Package (ASP) by two years.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Introduced in Budget 2016, the ASP supports firms to deploy impactful, large-scale automation, such as robotics, Internet of Things (IoT) solutions, and other Industry 4.0 technologies.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Since its launch, the ASP has helped more than 300 companies to automate their operations and raise productivity.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will extend the ASP to encourage more companies to do so.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR) will extend its operation and technology road-mapping efforts to more companies and sectors to guide them to make the best use of technology in alignment with their business goals.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the same spirit, our Government agencies must embrace technology to serve companies better.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Business Grants Portal launched in 2017 provides a one-stop shop for businesses to identify and apply for the right grant for their plans.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To make it easier for businesses to transact with the Government, the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI), and relevant agencies are developing a one-stop portal, with a pilot to be launched for the food services sector by the third quarter of 2019.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Businesses will deal with only one point of contact, instead of up to the 14 different ones today.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Building and Construction Authority (BCA) and the Housing Development Board (HDB) are also testing the use of drones to inspect building facades more effectively.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Learning from these pilots, Government agencies will continue to innovate, and improve the ease of doing business.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have more than 200,000 enterprises in Singapore, ranging from large multinational corporations (MNCs) to our neighbourhood shops.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Today, across each of the four pillars of our ITMs, different agencies provide support in each area.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: While helpful, companies have given feedback that we could streamline these.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To better support this broad base of companies with diverse needs, we will draw resources from each agency, but focus support in an enterprise-centric way to better help enterprises at each stage of growth.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will be done in a tiered manner.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Firms with large and complex needs or with strong growth potential will be provided a range of customised support by the Economic Development Board (EDB), Enterprise Singapore, and other agencies.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The large numbers of SMEs facing common challenges will be supported through scalable solutions that are easy to adopt.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For instance, I recently visited Precursor Assurance, a local accounting firm.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Precursor has developed an integrated digital solution with modules for corporate functions, such as HR, customer relationship management, and finance.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: SMEs can simply plug-and-play and scale up the use of these modules when they expand.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For medium-sized companies that are seeking to grow, we will provide targeted support, in each of the different industry clusters to better address their needs as they grow.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Minister for Trade and Industry will provide further details.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have touched on the measures to support our enterprises to build deep capabilities so that they can succeed in the global competition.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But our ultimate goal is to enable our people to continue to have good jobs and opportunities, and to be at their best.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Hence, the second thrust of our economic transformation in this Budget is to deepen the capabilities of our workers.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our people need to be nimble to build industry-relevant skills throughout their lives.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We want our people to have the skills, knowledge, and attitude to adapt and thrive in this competitive and technology-intensive environment.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In this regard, the leadership of companies plays a key role.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The leaders of successful companies are those who are committed to raising the capabilities of their workers by redesigning jobs and reskilling their staff.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These capabilities are key to the companies’ successes.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I recently visited FairPrice’s distribution centre, which has adopted automated storage and retrieval systems to improve the efficiency of its online store’s operations.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Among the staff I spoke to were Mr Amzah bin Mohammad Ali and Mdm Lee Yin Fong.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Between them, they have worked at FairPrice for 30 years.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I asked how the new technology has impacted their work.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They told me that FairPrice's training has helped them to quickly pick up new skills to make use of new systems, and their work environment is more pleasant and conducive.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: FairPrice is a good example of how an enterprise can strive to serve her customers better, deploy technology and new ways of working, and at the same time, redesign jobs and reskill workers so that everyone is better off.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many enterprises are doing this, and I urge more to take this approach.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: On the part of the Government, we will continue to invest in our people across all stages of their lives, from preschool to work.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Over the years, we have instituted a range of support measures for workers, including the Workfare Income Supplement (WIS), Special Employment Credit (SEC), and Professional Conversion Programmes (PCPs), to name a few.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These range from helping low-wage workers and older workers through wage support, to equipping young graduates to have a good start in their careers and enabling experienced professionals to access new jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In particular, NTUC has been working closely with its member unions and companies to enable workers to learn new skills and grow.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With the national SkillsFuture movement and the Adapt and Grow initiatives, we have made a stronger push to enable our people to reach their fullest potential throughout life, and help Singaporeans affected by restructuring.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our people are making good effort to invest in their learning, with good outcomes.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Workers, firms, unions, and TACs all need to play a part to continue this progress.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Workers need to embrace upskilling and reskilling and make the most of new opportunities both locally and overseas.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Firms must step up training and job redesign for their workers, as they are well placed to know the skills that workers need as their sectors evolve.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: One example is Mr Abdul Jalil Bin Idros, who started as a technical officer at YTL PowerSeraya.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Over the years, the company sponsored his Bachelor’s and Master's degrees in Electrical Engineering.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Through continuous learning as he worked, Mr Abdul Jalil moved from maintenance to managing plant upgrading projects.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: He is now training his colleagues in cybersecurity and systems operations.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: He received the SkillsFuture Fellowships Award in 2018 for his exemplary efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Besides workers and firms, unions, TACs and professional bodies need to spearhead the reskilling and the upskilling of workers in various sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I am heartened by the Institute of Singapore Chartered Accountants' collaboration with the Singapore University of Social Sciences (SUSS) to develop the joint Business Analytics Certification programme.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This programme, which was launched a year ago, equips accounting professionals with practical skills in data analytics.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will continue to enable our experienced professionals to build on their experience to move into new growth areas.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In 2015, we launched the Career Support Programme to provide wage support for employers to hire eligible Singaporeans who are mature and retrenched or are in long-term unemployment.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will extend this programme for two years.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must also ensure that the benefits of enterprise transformation are passed on to our workers.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I know that NTUC and the unions are putting in extra effort and resources to support our firms and workers in this.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Although some firms have done well to deploy their staff efficiently, productivity growth has been uneven across sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The manufacturing sector, which faces strong global competition, has done well.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the services sector, while some firms have done well despite a tight labour market, some segments like the food and beverage (F&B) and retail remain very labour-intensive.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Growth in S Pass and Work Permit holders in the services sector has also been picking up pace.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In particular, the S Pass growth in services is the highest in five years.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: If this trend persists, foreign manpower growth may will be on an unsustainable path.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We need to act decisively to manage the manpower growth in services, and encourage our companies to revamp work processes, redesign jobs, and reskill our workers.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our workforce growth is tapering, and if we do not use this narrow window to double down on restructuring, our companies will find it this even harder in the future.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Relying on more and more foreign workers is not the long-term solution – other economies are developing too.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: What we need is to have a sustainable inflow of foreign workers to complement our workforce, while we upgrade our Singaporean workers and build deep enterprise capabilities in these sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must enhance the complementarities of our local and foreign workers.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The basic approach to our foreign worker policies has remained consistent.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Based on evidence on the pace of foreign worker inflows, and the progress being made in raising productivity across sectors, we need to calibrate our policies.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government recognises the economic headwinds and cost pressures ahead of us.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But if we do not take action early, our firms will find it harder to compete in the years ahead, and our workers will be left behind.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are announcing these changes about a year ahead, to give companies time to prepare.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For firms whose existing workers are in excess of the new limits, the DRC will apply as and when these firms apply for renewals of permits.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To support firms as they adjust to these changes, we will put in place the following measures, till FY2022.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Separately, firms can continue to apply for additional manpower flexibilities in certain cases.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Lean Enterprise Development Scheme provides support to firms that undertake transformation projects which lead to more manpower-lean businesses.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Transitional manpower flexibilities can be considered if firms need more resources in the short term to transit to new operating models.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: On a case-by-case basis, firms can bring in foreign workers with specialised skills that are in demand globally.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is provided that they still face a shortage after having given fair consideration to Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Minister for Trade and Industry and the Minister for Manpower will provide more details at the COS.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have spoken on how Budget 2019 supports the building of deep enterprise capabilities, and the building of deep worker capabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To succeed, companies need to both compete and cooperate – compete to differentiate themselves and cooperate to solve common challenges.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our TACs can play an important role in developing industry-wide capabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This includes supporting members in getting business advice and improving access to local and international networks.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: TACs have done well in helping our companies build overseas partnerships.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, the Singapore FinTech Association has forged many partnerships with foreign FinTech associations, and the Singapore Business Federation (SBF) has organised Singapore’s commercial participation at numerous overseas trade fairs, including the 2018 China International Import Expo.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Singapore Chinese Chamber of Commerce and Industry has also developed the Trade Association Hub, which now houses 39 TACs, to raise the level of services for members.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: SBF is also working closely with our TACs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will strengthen our support for TACs through the Local Enterprise and Association Development (LEAD) programme.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Enterprise Singapore will be developing five-year roadmaps with TACs that have demonstrated strong leadership and shown ambition to do more for the business community.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will enable them to take on a more strategic and longer-term approach in driving industry transformation.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These TACs will be able to access funding and potentially take in public sector secondees through LEAD.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will also develop stronger partnerships around the world, at the Government-to-Government and Business-to-Business levels.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our TACs, such as the SBF, have developed international linkages for our businesses.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Over the years, we have negotiated Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) with partner economies, which enlarge our businesses’ access to new markets.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To draw greater value from these trade networks, we will streamline and digitise our trade processes further to raise efficiency.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will enable easier access to overseas markets, and help our firms make better use of these FTAs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will also be working with partners to facilitate the secure exchange of electronic trade documents, to unlock further productivity gains.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Members will appreciate that the three key thrusts I have just announced – building deep capabilities in our enterprises, in our people, and forging deep partnerships – build on the ITMs that I announced in Budget 2016.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With the progress we have made, we are better prepared for major changes that are coming our way.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: One major change is the speed of advancements and convergence of new technologies – it is what some have dubbed the Fourth Industrial Revolution or Industry 4.0.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will transform the way we invest, trade, and consume.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Over the years, we have forged deep partnerships with the G3 economies of US, Europe and Japan, as well as China, India and ASEAN.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With the centre of economic gravity shifting to Asia, and with the technological depth of our partnerships with the G3 economies, we should position Singapore as “Asia 101” for global MNCs looking to expand into Asia’s growing markets, and as “Global 101” for Asian companies ready to go global.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For our next phase of growth, as we press on with industry transformation, we will continue to build Singapore’s position as a Global-Asia node of technology, innovation and enterprise.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will open up new opportunities for our firms and our people to ride on the wave of the Fourth Industrial Revolution.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our efforts to achieve this will build on the same three key thrusts as laid out for the broader economic transformation: first, investments in research and innovation by our universities, research institutes, and our firms; second, investments in our people; and third, building global partnerships.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our investments in research and development (R&D) in our universities and research institutes are bearing fruit.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The National University of Singapore (NUS) and the Nanyang Technological University (NTU) are ranked the best in Asia in areas such as materials science and chemistry, and among the top 50 globally for engineering and computer science.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many of our researchers are regarded by their peers as among the world’s best, especially in areas such as AI, quantum technologies, and biomedical sciences.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A*STAR has research institutes that are highly regarded.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Together with our universities, they are actively working to translate research findings into innovation, in partnerships with industries.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But for R&D to make an impact, our companies must take the lead.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Members of this House will be encouraged to know that some sectors are moving ahead – including two “old economy” sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, despite digital advancements, we still need brick-and-mortar buildings.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The construction sector, seen as low-tech and labour-intensive, is now using Integrated Digital Delivery.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This makes use of Building Information Modelling and other digital technologies, connecting different players working on the same construction projects.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This has raised productivity and created new high-value jobs such as 3D modellers.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, in the digital age, we still need food, not just bits and bytes.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The agriculture and food production sectors are transforming.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, the Agri-Food and Veterinary Authority of Singapore's (AVA) Marine Aquaculture Centre and Temasek Life Sciences Laboratory have developed the "St John's Sea Bass".

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This fish is less susceptible to disease and can be bred in 30% less time.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A start-up, Allegro Aqua, is looking to bring more St John's Sea Bass to the world.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Another example is Temasek Life Sciences Laboratory's "Temasek Rice", which produces four times as much rice per hectare as compared to regular breeds of rice.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Leading MNCs and our large local companies are also establishing their R&D centres in Singapore in different areas of technology.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We now have 14 corporate laboratories in our universities, doing cutting-edge work ranging from cyber-physical systems to power electronics.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I recently visited LUX Photonics Consortium, which brings together researchers in NUS, NTU, A*STAR, and the industry, to translate cutting-edge photonics research into practical applications.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There, I met Nanoveu, a Singapore start-up specialising in nanotechnology applications.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: One of its prototype products, a high-tech screen protector, promises to allow long-sighted users to see clear images on digital devices without their glasses.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And to see 3D objects from 2D films, that is another project.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I am sure this House will support the enabling of us to see issues, far or near, with greater clarity and perspective!

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our Helix Bridge and new buildings such as the Jewel at Changi Airport are lit in scintillating ways by Technolite.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The company is embarking on R&D to take its products to a new level.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, I wish Nanoveu and Technolite success, to light up our lives and to let us see better!

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This Centre will bring together aquaculture firms to improve our food resilience.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The centre will collaborate with the Sustainable Energy Association of Singapore to drive industry-led innovation in areas such as energy efficiency, renewable energy, and electric mobility.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will share more about these exciting new research initiatives at the Research, Innovation and Enterprise Council meeting next month.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The spirit of entrepreneurship is critical for all these endeavours – having a vision of the future, and taking practical actions, day in, day out, to explore a range of possibilities and solve a myriad of problems.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is the grit and determination of our entrepreneurs that make a difference.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mr Sim Wong Hoo, CEO of Creative Technology, brought us the popular Sound Blaster cards in the 1990s.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Creative Technology went through a difficult patch after its initial success with the Sound Blaster, but Mr Sim and his team pressed on.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: After 20 years of R&D costing US$100 million, the company recently launched the Super X-Fi, a technology that recreates the holographic sound experience – or 3D sound – with headphones, personalised.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It has already won 14 awards at the 2019 Consumer Electronics Show in the US.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Having tried it myself, and having heard the endorsement of audiophiles, including some in this Chamber, I am happy that Mr Sim and his team are at the cusp of a major breakthrough.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mr Sim’s story illustrates the point that to succeed, we must learn, we must walk the ground, and we must persist.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have touched on our efforts in Research, Innovation, and Enterprise.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singapore as a Global-Asia node will bring new opportunities for our people, in new frontiers.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The second thrust is to prepare and develop our people to make full use of this node.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are partnering firms to invest in our people, including young Singaporeans, to provide them with opportunities to gain working experience abroad.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It will have enhanced funding support for our students interning overseas with Singapore firms.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: By giving young Singaporeans overseas exposure, they can develop new skills to better support our firms' overseas expansion.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For instance, Oceanus Group, a local seafood supplier, sent interns from Republic Polytechnic to its operations in China in a range of jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: One of their former interns, Bernice Chan, is now a management trainee in Oceanus' farm in Fotan, China.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our third thrust is to build global partnerships, so that our firms and people can forge new areas of collaboration with other innovation centres.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In Budget 2017, we started the Global Innovation Alliance (GIA), one of the Committee on the Future Economy's recommendations.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have now established nine nodes in global start-up hotspots such as Bangkok, Beijing, Berlin, Jakarta, and San Francisco.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These GIA nodes give our entrepreneurs and students opportunities to learn and build networks globally.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are also bringing the global innovation community to come together in Singapore, to explore and collaborate.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Last year, we held the third edition of the Singapore FinTech Festival.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is now the world's largest fintech event.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Another technology event, the Singapore Week of Innovation and Technology (SWITCH) brought together more than 350 exhibitors, and 1,000 promising start-ups and financiers from 75 countries.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To maximise impact, this year, SWITCH and the Singapore FinTech Festival will be held in the same week in mid-November.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We can draw in even more entrepreneurs, investors, innovators from around the world to explore and collaborate in technology innovation in this Fourth Industrial Revolution.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These various programmes on economic transformation and jobs build upon our efforts and investments over the years.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To summarise, our economic transformation is progressing well.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But, we must persist with our industry transformation efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: At the same time, the pace of technological innovation is rapid, and global economic weight is shifting towards Asia.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But let me emphasise that supporting companies and supporting workers are mutually reinforcing – stronger companies provide better jobs and pay for workers, and highly skilled workers make companies stronger.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I am confident that we can continue to make good progress.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our enterprises and TACs, workers and unions, and the Government must continue to work closely together.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As long as we stay relevant and useful to the world, we can continue to create opportunities for our people and enterprises.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have spoken about how we invest to secure our home and grow our economy.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: At the heart of these efforts is the desire to improve the lives of current and future generations of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our approach to social development has served us well.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We invest heavily to bring out the best in our people.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We believe that access to quality education enables Singaporeans to realise their potential.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We strive to ensure that all Singaporeans, regardless of background, enjoy a quality living environment and have good access to healthcare.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And we provide targeted support to those who are less advantaged, so that they too can have a fair chance to succeed; and to those who fall on hard times, so they can bounce back.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our efforts were affirmed by the World Bank when they ranked Singapore top in the Human Capital Index last year.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We recognise that Singapore, like many advanced economies, will have to deal with issues such as: (a) maintaining social mobility; (b) supporting healthy and purposeful ageing; and (c) fostering a stronger sense of unity amid polarising forces.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Over the past decade or so, we have significantly increased our social spending.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The social measures in Budget 2019 are part of our long-term plan to build a caring and inclusive society.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, uplifting Singaporeans to maximise their potential and to provide access to opportunities through their stages of life.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We pay particular attention to children from disadvantaged backgrounds, to give them a good start in life.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With increasing lifespans, we are helping older Singaporeans stay in the workforce, so that they can earn and save more for retirement.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will continue to strengthen support for the healthcare needs of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In particular, we want to help our seniors stay active, healthy and engaged in their silver years.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Third, fostering a community of care and contribution through strong partnerships.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We strive to nurture an ethos in our society where we support one another, giving a helping hand where we can.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Those who succeed should help to uplift others, just as they have benefited from the support of others around them.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are in the same boat, and weather the storms together.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We progress together and forge our future together.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will first talk about how we are supporting our children, workers, and seniors to access the best opportunities, through each stage of life.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We invest heavily to provide a world-class education for young Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is to bring out the best in every child, no matter his or her starting point.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I know that this is an area of deep concern for many Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many of you expressed this during feedback sessions, and through your actions in giving time and money to help children in need.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Preschools support parents in laying a strong foundation for children – by helping to develop children’s cognitive, language, social and emotional skills.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Therefore, we are spending more to enhance the accessibility, affordability, and quality of early childhood education and care.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And this support continues throughout the schooling years.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Children from lower-income families get even more support, for example, through the recently enhanced Ministry of Education (MOE) Financial Assistance Scheme.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have been doing more to better support children from disadvantaged backgrounds, by intervening earlier, with new forms of proactive and targeted support.One such effort is KidSTART.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: KidSTART practitioners, preschools, and community partners work together to provide health, learning, and developmental support for children and their families.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Last year, we set up the Uplifting Pupils in Life and Inspiring Families Taskforce (UPLIFT).

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This taskforce will pilot upstream interventions and partner communities to help disadvantaged children and their families, to ensure that no child is left behind.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The taskforce is also looking at how to strengthen after-school care and support for disadvantaged students in school-based Student Care Centres.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Minister for Education will speak about this, and other initiatives spurred by UPLIFT at the Committee of Supply (COS) debates.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our support for Singaporeans continues into their working lives.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Workfare and Silver Support is a key pillar of our social security system.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The two schemes supplement incomes and mitigate inequality in the working and retirement years respectively.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) scheme provides cash payouts and CPF top-ups for workers whose earnings are in the bottom 20%, with some support for those slightly above.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The scheme has raised their incomes, encouraged employment, and helped them save more for retirement.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will enhance WIS to better support lower-wage workers.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Older workers will see higher increases in payouts.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As our society ages, older workers will make up an increasing share of our workforce.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Today, about one in four of our workforce is aged 55 and above.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They continue to make important contributions to our economy and society.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some are giving back by mentoring the younger generations, while others wish to continue working.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are doing more to help older Singaporeans earn more, save more, and have greater peace of mind during their retirement years.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I appreciate the concerns and suggestions regarding the retirement adequacy of older workers, raised by members of the public and the PAP Seniors Group, among others.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And I thank the Members of this House for your views during the recent debate on the motions on ageing with purpose and support for caregivers.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government has set up a Tripartite Workgroup to study the concerns of older workers.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Workgroup is reviewing policies such as the retirement and re-employment age, and the CPF contribution rates of older workers.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They will present their recommendations later this year.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To support employers in hiring older Singaporean workers, the Government introduced the Special Employment Credit (SEC) scheme in 2011.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Since then, we have extended and made changes to the SEC in response to labour market and economic conditions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have also introduced an Additional SEC (ASEC) scheme to encourage employers to hire workers who are above the re-employment age.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With a tighter labour market and more Singaporeans choosing to work longer, more companies will be hiring older workers.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government will study better forms of support to continue to help workers to remain productive, earn more, and save more for retirement.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will review the relevance and structure of the SEC and ASEC, in tandem with the recommendations from the Tripartite Workgroup on Older Workers.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the meantime, I will extend the SEC and ASEC for another year, until 31 December 2020.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To support this extension, I will top up the SEC Fund by $366 million.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Taken together, Members will see that the Government has been making significant investments in education and employment for our people, from early childhood to the working years.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our aim is to help Singaporeans fulfil their potential at each stage of life.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are improving the lives of our people by enabling them to be the best that they can be.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We enhance our people’s sense of well-being and dignity, without the burden of welfare schemes elsewhere, which weaken people's sense of agency and independence.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As more Singaporeans enter their senior years, healthcare needs will grow.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Over the years, we have implemented major changes to make healthcare more affordable, accessible, and comprehensive.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have also been providing greater social support within the community to help seniors stay active, through programmes, such as the PA Wellness Programme and the Community Networks for Seniors.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our second social strategy is to provide greater healthcare assurance.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, doctors at our neighbourhood clinics provide primary care that is easily accessible.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To enhance access, we will make it more affordable to consult doctors in our neighbourhoods.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We introduced the Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS) in 2012.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: CHAS subsidies help lower- to middle-income families by making primary care and basic dental care at clinics near their homes more affordable.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: CHAS makes it possible for more Singaporeans to turn to GP clinics near their homes to manage their chronic conditions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But we must also put in the measures to ensure that CHAS clinics are delivering good outcomes.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To this end, the Ministry of Health (MOH) will be looking at how to help CHAS clinics better track their patients' progress and outcomes.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In a similar vein, MOH will also review its clinical guidelines for care provided at CHAS dental clinics, to ensure that the care delivered is appropriate to the needs of the patient.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Minister for Health will provide more details on these changes at the Committee of Supply (COS) debates.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A second way to provide greater healthcare assurance is that we will strengthen financial protection for long-term care.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As we age, the chances of having one form of disability or another rises significantly.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: MOH estimates that one in two healthy Singaporeans aged 65 could become severely disabled in their lifetime and may need long-term care.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some of us face a higher risk, some lower.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But regardless, "low risk" does not mean "no risk".

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The best way of protecting ourselves is to lead a healthy lifestyle and take preventive actions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: At the same time, we need to guard against unpredictable events.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The most efficient way is to help one another, by pooling risk through an insurance scheme.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Today, we have MediShield Life, for all Singaporeans, to provide financial protection against large hospital bills for life.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As we live longer, there is a higher chance that we will need long-term care towards the end of our lives.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Ministry of Health (MOH) has announced that it will be introducing the new CareShield Life from 2020, an enhancement of the current ElderShield scheme.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This offsets the costs of long-term care for individuals and their families.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government will provide subsidies and premium support to ensure that CareShield Life premiums are affordable.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will also offer participation incentives for existing cohorts, born in 1979 or earlier, to join CareShield Life, so that they are better protected should they need care in the future.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: CareShield Life will offer much greater peace of mind for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In addition, we will also launch ElderFund next year to help severely disabled, lower-income Singaporeans who need additional financial support for long-term care.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This includes those who might not be able to join CareShield Life, or have low MediSave balances.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The cost of long-term care is not only high, but will increase as our population ages.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will help fund the CareShield Life subsidies and other long-term care support measures, such as ElderFund.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is a significant commitment to help Singaporeans with their long-term care needs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As the Prime Minister mentioned at the National Day Rally last year and the Tribute event earlier this month, we would also like to express our appreciation and support for our Merdeka Generation.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Merdeka Generation is a resilient and independent generation.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They played a critical role in our nation's development.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Merdeka Generation was among the earliest batches to serve National Service, build up our public services, and modernise our economy.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They came together to forge our multicultural and multiracial society.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: One member of the Merdeka Generation is Ms Barbara D' Cotta.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Ms D' Cotta started work as a special education teacher at the age of 19 to help support her mother.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In 1984, she was among the first batch of teachers to attain a Certificate in Special Education.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Throughout her life, she continued learning, and completed her Bachelor in Special Education in 2016, at the age of 57!

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Today, she is a Specialised Teacher for students with hearing deficiencies and a volunteer interpreter.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: She is also pursuing her Master of Special Education.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: She is an excellent example of lifelong learning and giving.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I am glad to have met Ms D' Cotta and many others who built our nation at our Merdeka Generation Tribute event.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They continue to be an active generation, contributing in their various capacities – at work, in the community, caring for their families, and learning something new.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Merdeka Generation Package is a gesture of our nation's gratitude for their contributions and a way to show care for them in their silver years.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It will provide them better peace of mind over future healthcare costs, while helping them to stay active and healthy.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Merdeka Generation Package (MGP) comprises five key benefits.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They can use this to pay for activities and facilities at the community clubs, entry to public swimming pools, public transport, and more.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will also work to introduce more active ageing opportunities for seniors, such as lifelong learning under the National Silver Academy and volunteerism under the Silver Volunteer Fund.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will start from this year until 2023.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will help them save more for their healthcare needs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is on top of the GST Voucher – MediSave top-ups that eligible seniors aged 65 and above receive every year.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They will receive special CHAS subsidies, for common illnesses, chronic conditions, and dental procedures.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The subsidy rates will be higher than the CHAS Blue subsidies.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: All MG seniors will receive these enhanced subsidies, regardless of income, including those who do not have a CHAS card today.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: At polyclinics and public Specialist Outpatient Clinics, they will receive 25% off their subsidised bills.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is on top of the prevailing subsidies available.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: All MG seniors will receive subsidies for their premiums, starting from 5% of their MediShield Life premiums, and increasing to 10% after they reach 75 years of age.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is on top of the means-tested subsidies that lower- to middle-income Singaporeans are already receiving.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will cover a significant portion of their premiums, and is on top of the regular means-tested premium subsidies.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I hope that this will encourage our MG seniors to join CareShield Life, to have peace of mind against the risk of high long-term care costs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: (See Table D-1.) The Merdeka Generation Package will benefit close to 500,000 Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Those born in the 1950s and who obtained citizenship by 1996 will be eligible for the MGP.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In addition, we will extend the MGP benefits to those born in 1949 or earlier but missed out on the Pioneer Generation Package (PGP), if they obtained citizenship by 1996.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: All eligible seniors will receive the MGP benefits, regardless of their income.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They will be notified by April 2019, and will receive their Merdeka Generation cards starting from June 2019.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Minister for Health will provide further details and the implementation timeline for the MGP benefits at the COS.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Merdeka Generation is aged 60 to 69 today.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singaporeans' lifespans are increasing – our life expectancy is now 84.8 years.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It also means the Merdeka Generation will be able to enjoy the benefits for many years.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
