text: This Budget, I will set aside $6.1 billion for a new Merdeka Generation Fund.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With interest accumulated over time, this will cover the full projected costs of the Merdeka Generation Package.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Merdeka Generation will enjoy many key healthcare benefits for life.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We hope that this will go some way in providing greater peace of mind for the Merdeka Generation and their families.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is a significant commitment by the Government.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is important that the Government of the day continues to monitor the patterns and cost of healthcare utilisation, and life expectancy over the next 30 years or more, so that the Government is able to meet this commitment.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To better prepare for increasing lifespans, we should encourage everyone to set aside something for the future.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To help Singaporeans who are younger than the Merdeka Generation with their future healthcare expenses, I will provide MediSave top-up of $100 a year, for the next five years, for Singaporeans who are aged 50 and above in 2019; and who do not receive the MGP or the PGP.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is a generation who are even younger and healthier, and I hope that everyone will make the extra effort to stay active and healthy.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our third social strategy is to foster a community of care and contribution and build strong partnerships in our society.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government will continue to make every effort to care for our seniors, the disadvantaged, and vulnerable families.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The ComCare Long-Term Assistance scheme provides basic monthly cash assistance to those who are permanently unable to work and have little family support to support their living expenses.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Additional assistance is provided for households with additional needs, such as medical supplies.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will raise the cash assistance rates for this scheme.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, a two-person household, where both are on ComCare Long-Term Assistance, will receive an additional $130 a month.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This brings the total cash assistance to $1,000 a month.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Minister for Social and Family Development will provide more details at the COS.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To help Government pensioners who draw lower pensions, we will increase the Singapore allowance and monthly pension ceiling by $20 per month each, to $320 and $1,250 respectively.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Working alongside the Government, individuals, non-profit organisations, and corporates have all been playing their part – contributing their skills, their time, and their hearts.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As we reflect on our history and culture in this bicentennial year, we see this spirit of helping one another as a community in action over time.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the past, our forefathers who arrived in Singapore banded together mainly within their ethnic groups, forming various clans and associations, as the support of the Government then was inadequate.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Today, I am glad that this spirit extends across ethnic and religious lines in our society.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the last few months, we have received many good suggestions from members of the public on cultivating this community spirit to help those in need.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As our society ages and new needs emerge, we hope everyone will lend a helping hand.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: One good example is Mr Shaleem Khamalluden and his friends from PALS Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: PALS stands for Peace and Love Society, a non-profit organisation that provides a support network for Singaporean youths from all backgrounds.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Through sports events and workshops, Shaleem and other like-minded volunteers have been helping young Singaporeans learn skills to overcome challenges such as bullying and cyber-addiction.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To date, they have touched the lives of about 800 youths.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Another example is Dr Rose Sivam, who started My Home, Your Home.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With her husband as the chef, Rose and her family bring together people from various backgrounds, including those with disabilities and children with special needs, to share a meal in her home.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is another good example of our community spirit – how we care for the less privileged and build unity in our diversity.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I am heartened that many other Singaporeans, too, have stepped forward in their own ways to make a difference within their community, and I encourage everyone to do their part.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I spoke about the SG Cares movement at last year’s Budget.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It seeks to bring together the public, people, and private sectors in partnership, create a greater collective impact and grow as a community of care and contribution.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This year, we continue to build on the SG Cares movement.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will have three measures to mobilise our people across all age groups, and across the public, private, and people sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First is growing the spirit of volunteerism in our youth.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many of our secondary school students are already active volunteers and are giving back to the community.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, our seniors have an abundance of skills and experience to make meaningful contributions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will also enable our seniors to stay active and contribute to the community, at work and when they retire.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Today, each Ministry has a senior officer appointed as the Giving Ambassador to champion volunteerism.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Going forward, Public Service Cares will strengthen capabilities in Corporate Social Responsibility and create larger-scale and sustained volunteering opportunities for public officers across agencies.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, they can take part in house visits to share healthcare and active ageing schemes, or guide seniors in using their mobile devices at digital clinics.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will also help Public Service officers to better understand citizens' needs, and co-deliver services with the people and private sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is the Public Service's contribution to the SG Cares movement.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth will be sharing more on SG Cares at the COS.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The spirit of giving back has a special meaning this year, as we commemorate the Singapore Bicentennial.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Therefore, I will launch two special initiatives in support of this.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Today, we encourage individuals and corporates to give back to the community in various ways.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Donations to Institutions of a Public Character (IPCs) qualify for a 250% tax deduction.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Businesses also enjoy a 250% tax deduction on qualifying expenditure when their employees volunteer or provide services to IPCs under the Business and IPC Partnership Scheme.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With this, we hope to further encourage more Singaporeans, including younger Singaporeans, to embrace the spirit of giving back.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: At the same time, we are encouraging IPCs to reach out to more donors.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The fund will be designed to ensure a good distribution of support for all donations to IPCs which currently do not receive Government matching, and to increase the impact of the good work they are doing.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have also enhanced our one-stop platform, Giving.sg, to better match donors and volunteers with meaningful causes.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This platform provides charities with an easy and secure way to establish an online presence, and to receive donations digitally.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Donors, too, can quickly navigate and find a worthy cause that matches their passion and commitment, and start on their giving journey.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Details will be shared by the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY) at a later date.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: From time to time, when our finances allow, we share the surpluses with Singaporeans, and provide more help to those with specific needs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With this Bonus, I hope that all Singaporeans, young and old, will join us to commemorate this significant moment in Singapore's history.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have set the cap at $200 so that the benefits go mostly to middle-income earners.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For parents with school-going children, we will provide additional support for their children's education.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Each year, the Government contributes to the Edusave accounts of all Singaporean students at primary and secondary school levels.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is on top of the annual Edusave contributions that they already receive from the Government.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In addition, Singaporeans aged 17 to 20 will receive up to $500 in their Post-Secondary Education Accounts (PSEA).

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will go towards helping parents to save for their children’s tertiary education.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will be credited into the Special Account for members aged 50 to 54, and the Retirement Account for members aged 55 to 64.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: About 300,000 Singaporeans will benefit from this CPF top-up.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The majority of these recipients will be women.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many of them left the workforce early, and took up important roles as mothers, caregivers, or housewives.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As a result, they had fewer years to build up their savings.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This top-up is a way to recognise their contributions and to help them save more.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In addition to the CPF top-up, Singaporeans in the age group of 50 to 64 who qualify for Workfare will also benefit from the WIS enhancements that I mentioned earlier.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Most of those in the 60 to 64 age group will also receive the Merdeka Generation Package, while the rest will receive the five-year MediSave top-ups.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These are all on top of the targeted benefits such as the GST Voucher.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Together, we hope that these measures will provide greater peace of mind for our older workers now and later in their silver years.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In addition to the special Bicentennial initiatives, we will provide another year of Service and Conservancy Charges (S&CC) Rebate to HDB households.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Eligible Singaporean households will receive S&CC rebates of between 1.5 months and 3.5 months.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will cost $132 million and benefit about 930,000 households.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government keeps a close watch on the cost of living.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Over the years, we have done much to alleviate cost pressures – whether in healthcare, education, or day-to-day expenses.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Good macroeconomic management has enabled us to keep inflation low, while the Singapore dollar has been strengthening over time.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many Singaporeans who go on overseas vacations would appreciate this.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Over and above these favourable conditions, this Budget continues to provide significant support for Singaporeans, especially our seniors and lower-income households.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Budget 2019 supports the Government’s long-term strategy to build a caring and inclusive society.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is our continued effort to improve the lives of our people and our future generations.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Today, our shining little red dot can hold its own on the global stage.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But as the Minister for National Development has said, "we are not done building Singapore".

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Infrastructure takes time to build, but once built, can serve us for a long time.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must take a long view for our development plans.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The upcoming Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA) Master Plan 2019 will guide our urban development over a 10- to 15-year time frame.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It ensures that our limited land can be optimised to meet the needs of current and future generations.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Minister for National Development will share more details at the COS.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The long-term transformation of our city must start with our HDB estates, where most Singaporeans’ homes are.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is important that we keep our living environment first-class.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many cities have large tracts that slip into disrepair over time – we must avoid that.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must strive to make every town in Singapore green and liveable, by rejuvenating them systematically over time.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As our home, and a global node, our city has to be well-connected within and with the world.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Within Singapore, we now have about 230 kilometres of MRT lines.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will rise to about 360 kilometres in the 2030s when major MRT projects, such as the Cross Island Line are completed.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To enhance our global connectivity, we are increasing the capacities of our airport and seaport.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will strengthen our role as a key node within Asia and to the world.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Connecting to future growth, knowledge, and cultural centres in Asia and beyond will not only benefit Singaporeans, but also add to the connectivity and vibrancy in our region.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Beyond the next decade, we must also plan for climate change.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Climate change and rising sea levels threaten our very existence.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As a low-lying island nation, there is nowhere to hide when sea levels rise.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Other small island nations like the Maldives are already facing the risk of flooding, with severe implications The Government is studying the implications carefully and will come up with measures to prepare ourselves adequately.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In line with the Action Plan, low-lying roads near coastal areas have been raised.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These will help us to learn how to deal with rising sea levels.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To protect ourselves against climate change and rising sea levels, we will have to invest more.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Together with existing infrastructure needs, our total bill for infrastructure will increase significantly.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is very difficult to project spending needs way into the future, but the different Ministries have done some preliminary estimates.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will continue to do our best to look forward, develop fiscal plans well in advance, and put in place the right approach to finance such long-lived major infrastructure.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is the responsible thing to do for our children and future generations.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The carbon tax will be applied on this year's emissions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is an important signal to companies and households to reduce emissions and adopt energy-efficient practices.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As individuals, we too must change our ways and work towards becoming a zero-waste nation, by adopting the three "R"s: reducing consumption, reusing, and recycling.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Zero Waste Masterplan will be launched in the second half of this year.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Among other issues, it will look at better management of food waste, e-waste, and packaging waste including plastics.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources will provide more details at the COS.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Given our dense urban environment, air quality and greenery are especially important.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The National Parks Board (NParks) has done an excellent job in greening Singapore – our island has more than 40% green cover.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This improves our living environment and our air quality.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But diesel exhaust is highly pollutive and adversely affects our people's health and quality of life.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many cities in Europe have announced restrictions on diesel vehicle usage.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have taken steps to discourage diesel consumption.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Over the years, we have implemented schemes to encourage early renewal of diesel commercial goods vehicles and to also account for the impact of vehicular emissions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: More owners are shifting towards more environmentally-friendly engines such as electric hybrids.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are glad to see a drop in the numbers of new diesel cars and taxis registered.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We also restructured diesel taxes in 2017 to shift away from an annual amount of tax towards a usage-based tax system.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We permanently reduced the annual special tax on diesel cars and taxis, and re-introduced the volumetric diesel duty.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I strongly urge taxi companies to pass on the savings to their drivers, like they did in 2017.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will on average reduce the impact of the duty increase by more than three-quarters for taxis.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will also permanently reduce the Special Tax on diesel cars by $100.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will, on average, reduce the impact by more than half.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will also provide, over three years, additional cash rebates of up to $3,200 for diesel buses ferrying school children.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Building a more sustainable environment makes our quality of life better, and also creates economic opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Just as we closed the water loop, we can now turn our attention to closing the waste loop.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Two companies, UglyGood and Tria, have been working on innovative ways to convert food-related waste into useful products.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These are good examples of opportunities in our zero waste movement.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So I hope to see more of such initiatives in the coming years.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our beautiful living environment can also be enhanced through the smart use of technology, as a part of our Smart Nation efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To reduce energy use, we have implemented district cooling in the Marina Bay area.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To improve our quality of life, we have started rolling out pneumatic waste collection, and trialled smart urban mobility solutions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Buildings can also be designed to be environmentally friendly, for example, by being energy efficient and producing enough renewable energy to run itself.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Building and Construction Authority (BCA) was the first to retrofit its academy in 2009, making it the first retrofitted net-zero energy building in Southeast Asia.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This year, NUS’s School of Design and Environment launched SDE4, a brand-new net-zero energy building.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These initiatives contribute towards making our environment more sustainable and pleasant.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The National Research Foundation will continue to fund research and innovation in urban solutions and sustainability.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our public housing policies have also been uniquely successful because of our long-term planning.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Today, we are not just building new flats.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are improving the quality of life for Singaporeans through the rejuvenation of our public housing estates.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our plans for the rejuvenation and renewal of our city includes the Home Improvement Programme (HIP), the Neighbourhood Renewal Programme (NRP) and the Remaking Our Heartland (ROH) initiative.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For the longer term, we have announced HIP 2 and the Voluntary Early Redevelopment Scheme (VERS).

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These are plans that will keep our living environment first-class over the coming years.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Minister for National Development will be sharing more on these plans to build endearing homes for our people at the Committee of Supply (COS) debates.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singapore's ability to plan for the long term is our strategic advantage.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But the best-laid plans to develop our people and transform our city can only be realised with a sound fiscal plan.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our fiscal discipline and prudence gave us the resources to respond decisively to unexpected challenges, such as the 2008 Global Financial Crisis.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some of these are major, long-term projects, such as the development of Changi East and rail projects such as the Cross Island Line.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Others, such as infrastructure to protect us against climate change, are contingent on the future state of the world.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is challenging to predict their exact timing and requirements.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Borrowing, done in a responsible and sustainable manner, will help instil financial discipline and distribute the share of funding more equitably across current and future generations.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the 1980s, the Government borrowed to build our first MRT lines.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our Statutory Boards and Government-owned companies have also continued to finance many major infrastructure projects through borrowings.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For the development of Changi East, the Changi Airport Group will be taking up loans to fund its share of the infrastructure investments.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This allows us to tap on the strength of the Government's balance sheet to back this strategic investment.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government is further studying the option of using Government debt as part of the financing mix for long-term infrastructure projects that the Government will be taking on directly.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, for recurrent spending needs in areas such as healthcare, preschool education and security, we must recognise that these are necessary expenditures – to take care of our elderly, give our children a good start in life, and keep Singapore safe and secure for our families.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many countries have taken the easier route by funding these recurrent expenditures through borrowing.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must not do this, as such borrowing shifts the burden of paying for today's needs onto future generations.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A fairer and more robust approach is to meet recurrent spending with recurrent revenues.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Hence, we must continually review our tax system to ensure its resilience.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: GST is a broad-based tax that contributes significantly to our fiscal resources.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Last year, I announced the introduction of GST on imported services to make sure GST collections remain fair and resilient in a digital economy.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This year, I will tighten the GST import relief for travellers, given rising international travel.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will take effect from 1 April 2019.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As I had announced at the previous Budget, we will raise GST by two percentage points sometime in the period from 2021 to 2025.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: When we raise GST, we will ensure that our overall system of taxes and transfers remains progressive and fair.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will continue to absorb GST on publicly-subsidised education and healthcare.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will provide more help to lower-income households and the elderly by enhancing the permanent GST Voucher scheme.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will also cushion the impact of the GST increase for a period through a GST offset package.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Notwithstanding the need to raise revenues in the future, at the core of our fiscal system is our commitment to keep the overall tax burden low.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We want workers and firms to keep as much as possible of what they earn.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This leaves our citizens free to choose how they spend, save, or invest.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our main indirect tax, the GST, is not high by international standards, even after the planned increase to 9%.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Among the Asia Pacific countries, many have standard GST rates that exceed 9%.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Ultimately, a competitive tax regime helps us to attract and retain investments and talent.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These in turn help to bring in good jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A competitive tax regime is a key anchor to our economic growth, and the best way to sustainably increase tax revenues.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will extend and strengthen tax incentives to enhance our business competitiveness.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: At the same time, I will make some adjustments to further enhance the progressivity and resilience of our tax system.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The details of these changes are in the Annex.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government will continue to plan ahead for the long term.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: My commitment to Singaporeans is that our overall taxes and transfers system will always remain fair, progressive, and pro-growth.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: On the whole, we expect an overall Budget deficit of $3.5 billion, or 0.7% of GDP.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have sufficient fiscal surplus accumulated over this term of Government to fund the overall deficit in FY2019.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, I would like to thank the many Singaporeans, as well as businesses, unions, charities, and community organisations, who have provided your feedback and ideas.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Also, special thanks to the talented students from Nanyang Polytechnic for the beautiful sketches that you see in my slides today.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We commemorate 2019, our bicentennial year, to learn from our past in order to chart our future.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will have many opportunities to reflect and share in the coming months and years, but three lessons stand out for me and my colleagues.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, for as long as we stay relevant and useful, Singapore and Singaporeans will have our place in the world.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must develop deep capabilities, stay open and connected, and draw ideas and talents from around the globe.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singaporean talents have been making their mark in various fields, and connecting with other highly skilled individuals from around the world will make our team even stronger.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, external events around us will shape and reshape our lives.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our people have shown time and again that we can take the long view, adapt with the times, and thrive.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Third, we draw strength from our diversity by focusing on what we have in common.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the earlier years, our forefathers clustered around ethnic and religious groups to support one another.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Today, Singaporeans support one another, regardless of race, language, or religion.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We build on our multicultural heritage, to foster a caring and inclusive society.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We continue to nurture our young and develop our people on a lifelong basis.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We seek to take better care of our seniors so that they can stay active and healthy.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will partner businesses and workers to transform our economy.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We welcome the best MNCs and SMEs from around the world, and help our start-ups and SMEs to grow, scale, and internationalise.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will help our workers deepen their capabilities and seek new opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To catch the wave of the Fourth Industrial Revolution, we are positioning Singapore as a Global-Asia node of technology, innovation and enterprise.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The changes ahead will be faster and deeper.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Budget 2019 highlights the key challenges we are facing and how we are preparing to ride on the changes, to turn challenges into opportunities, for Singaporeans and for our partners in the global community.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are investing to keep Singapore safe and secure.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are restructuring our economy to enable our businesses and workers to thrive.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are building a more caring and inclusive society, and we are building Singapore as a global city and a home for all.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Even as we invest more, Budget 2019 maintains our fiscal discipline.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our institution of the Elected President, and the Council of Presidential Advisors, ensure that the Government of the day does not squander the reserves our forefathers have left for us.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government will ensure that we abide by this.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must not only take care of this generation, but our children and their children.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is a core value we must uphold.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Budget 2019 lays out this Government’s approach to build a strong, united Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We nurture our young, take care of our seniors, expand opportunities for our people to be at their best, and to live in a liveable, endearing home, secure and globally connected.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Together, in close partnership with all, in our public, people, and private sectors, we can, and will, continue to take Singapore forward.
